subject: Synthex parity probe & hallucination thresholds
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna.li@synthex.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.wu@synthex.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Synthex parity probe - clarifying next evaluation steps

Thanks again for the demo this morning — Tom and I appreciated the focus on real-world inference economics. We had a few follow-up asks from our MLQA and procurement teams so I'm summarizing here to keep things moving: 

- Can you share a short probe matrix that maps the tests you run against hyperscaler endpoints (latency percentiles, hallucination checks, token cost normalization)?
- We need to understand how Redwood reports hallucination — do you provide per-prompt flags, aggregated rates, and per-model deltas?
- Our procurement team wants a simple mutual action plan and a draft commercial term to validate budgeting (no binding yet).

I've attached Synthex's evaluation constraints (file: Synthex_eval-constraints.pdf) and a small sample dataset (probe-results-sample.csv) showing a few failing examples we saw on HyperscaleX. Could your team run the probe matrix (we're flexible on seed prompts) and come back with: 
  * expected 90th/95th latency on a 512-token request, 
  * hallucination rate on our closed-book QA set, and 
  * rough token-cost estimate normalized to HyperscaleX per 1M tokens?

Anna
Anna Li
Head of Applied ML, SynthexAI

Attachment: Synthex_eval-constraints.pdf (pdf), probe-results-sample.csv (csv)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Anna Li <anna.li@synthex.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Synthex parity probe - clarifying next evaluation steps

Anna — thanks for the clear ask and the sample set. This is exactly the kind of signal we want early in qualification. Quick readout / proposal below: 

Summary proposal (high level)
- We will run a focused parity probe comparing Redwood-hosted variants vs HyperscaleX and their public endpoint. Tests: latency P50/P90/P95 for 128/512 tokens, closed-book QA hallucination, prompt-sensitivity regression (10k prompts).
- Deliverables: a one-page results brief, the normalized token-cost model, and a short canary config for your sandbox traffic.

Target metrics (to align expectations)
- Latency: P95 target within 1.3x of HyperscaleX on equivalent GPU backends for 512-token workloads (we'll report actual numbers).
- Hallucination: we will compute per-prompt binary flags and aggregate an "answer-entropy" score; our suggested acceptance threshold is <= 2.0% factual hallucination on your closed-book QA set for parity. If Synthex needs a stricter threshold we can tune quantization/profile choices.
- Cost: we'll provide normalized cost per 1M tokens and a delta vs HyperscaleX, plus guidance on batching/cache knobs to hit cost targets.

Next steps / owners
1) Redwood runs parity probe and returns results brief (owner: ben_carter) — ETA Thu Apr 19 EOD PT.
2) Joint sandbox run to validate with your traffic subset (owner: jonas_weber) — target Mon Apr 22.
3) Procurement mutual action plan and draft term sheet from Redwood for initial commitment (owner: marissa_cole) — ETA Fri Apr 21.

I've attached a probe matrix template (Synthex_ProbeMatrix_v2.xlsx) to show exactly what we'll run. If Tom or your engineering team want any additional specific prompts included, send them to ben and we'll fold them in.

Onwards — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Synthex_ProbeMatrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Anna Li <anna.li@synthex.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.wu@synthex.ai, procurement@synthex.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Synthex parity probe - clarifying next evaluation steps

Thanks Sean — these owners and timelines work for us. Two clarifications from our side: 
- For hallucination measurement, can you provide both a strict "exact match" and a "fact-checker" label? Our reviewers like to see both numbers because some correct paraphrases fail exact-match but are still acceptable.
- Procurement asked for a one-page non-binding commercial that lists a short pilot price band and what constitutes sandbox traffic vs production. Marissa — is that something you can draft?

Tom also noted that for long-context scenarios (>2k tokens) we see different drift patterns — if you can include a short long-context probe (1000/2000 token sim) that would be helpful.

Anna

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Synthex qualification — proposed test matrix and differentiators

Folks — quick internal note before we run the probe tomorrow (Ben/Jonas please pick up items assigned below). I'm flagging a few Redwood differentiators we should highlight in the brief and a couple of added tests to make the comparison defensible: 

Key differentiators to call out
- Smart routing + fallback: show how we can failover to a cheaper variant rather than a single endpoint outage (include a short concrete example).
- KV-cache + prefix caching: demonstrate token-cost savings on repeated-session flows (include a small microbenchmark).
- Quantization profiles: show a latency/cost/quality Pareto for 8-bit vs 4-bit configs.

Additional tests to add to Ben's probe run
1) Long-context drift: sample runs at 1k/2k tokens with continuity-check prompts to surface hallucination drift.
2) Cache-bypass stress: run many short sessions to show per-request latency delta when cache cold vs warm.
3) Cost-per-conversation model: simulate 10k conversation sessions to provide an expected monthly burn.

Ben: run the extra tests and annotate any prompts where hallucination rises >1.5x vs HyperscaleX; collect raw per-prompt flags so we can produce a heatmap.
Jonas: prepare the sandbox canary config and a short runbook for Synthex engineering (how to key traffic, expected tokens per call, recommended batch sizes).
Marissa: I'll draft the non-binding commercial one-pager and share a DocuSign link for the pilot MSA redlines.

Marissa
VP, Solutions & GTM, Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, procurement@synthex.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Synthex parity probe — results brief & MAP (next steps)

Anna/Tom/procurement — attached is the brief from Ben (summary below) and a short mutual action plan (MAP) so procurement has clear milestones. High level findings: 

- Latency: Redwood P95 on 512-token closed-gen was 420ms vs HyperscaleX 380ms on the same GPU family (ratio ~1.11x). P50 was 160ms (HyperscaleX 145ms).
- Hallucination: Exact-match metric: Redwood 1.8% vs HyperscaleX 2.6% on your closed-book QA set. Fact-checker label: Redwood 3.1% vs HyperscaleX 4.4%. Both metrics include long-context probes where drift increases (we flagged specific prompts).
- Cost: normalized token cost shows Redwood at ~0.82x HyperscaleX with caching and batching enabled; cold-cache cost is ~1.05x. We included suggested batching/cache knobs for production.

Attachments included: probe brief (Synthex_probe_brief.pdf), raw per-prompt flags (probe-results-sample-annotated.csv), and the non-binding commercial one-pager (Synthex_pilot_onepager.pdf). 

Mutual Action Plan (summary)
- Redwood: Deliver sandbox canary + runbook (owner: jonas_weber) — ETA Mon Apr 22.
- Synthex: Provide final sandbox traffic subset and procurement contact (owner: Anna) — ETA Mon Apr 22.
- Redwood: DocuSign link for pilot MSA + pilot pricing (owner: marissa_cole) — ETA Fri Apr 21 (link shared).

Next asks from Synthex we should surface in the pilot
- Include both exact-match and fact-checker labels in the weekly quality reports.
- Run a two-week warm-cache sampling to validate cold vs warm differences on representative traffic.

Thanks team — I'll log the HubSpot activity and attach the Drive folder (link below). If procurement wants a short call to review the one-pager, we can schedule early next week.

Best — Sean

Attachments: Synthex_probe_brief.pdf (pdf), Synthex_probe_results-annotated.csv (csv), Synthex_pilot_onepager.pdf (pdf)
